title: Existence of a closed group embedding descends over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $L/F$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $G,H$ be affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type over $F$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $G_L,H_L$ be their scalar extensions [def-pc-base-change]. There exists a homomorphism of $F$-group schemes $j:G\to H$ that is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] if and only if there exists a homomorphism of $L$-group schemes $j':G_L\to H_L$ that is a closed immersion. The assertion concerns existence: $j$ need not have scalar extension equal to a given $j'$. No smoothness, reducedness or connectedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, parts (2)–(3), applied to finite-presentation affine group laws; combined with Algebra Tag 00FV, theorem-nullstellensatz, finite residue fields of maximal ideals of finite type F-algebras. Agent-formulated consequence for existence of an embedding.

proof.text: For the forward implication, base change a closed immersion $j:G\to H$ along $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. It remains a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Base change preserves its multiplication equation: the two induced maps from $G_L\times_LG_L$ have the same composites with the projections defining the fibre products, so are equal. Thus $j_L$ is a group homomorphism by [def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Tag 01QR, lemma-base-change-closed-immersion; base-change functoriality in Schemes Tag 01JX.

proof.text: For the reverse implication put $B=F[G]$ and $C=F[H]$. They are finitely generated $F$-algebras by [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra]. The field $F$ is Noetherian: a nonzero ideal contains a nonzero scalar and therefore $1$, so its ideals are generated by $0$ or $1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] to obtain finite presentations of both $B$ and $C$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the given $j'$ corresponds to an $L$-algebra map $u_L:C\otimes_FL\to B\otimes_FL$. It is surjective by the affine criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion].

Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated $F$-subalgebras $R\subseteq L$, ordered by inclusion. It contains $F$; adjoining the union of two finite generating sets gives an upper bound; every $\ell\in L$ belongs to $F[\ell]$. Hence $L=\varinjlim_{R\in I}R$ as rings: for a compatible cocone, send $\ell$ through any stage containing it; compatibility in a common stage gives independence, addition, multiplication and uniqueness. Write $B_R=B\otimes_FR$ and $C_R=C\otimes_FR$. Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-category-fp-algebras] at the initial stage $F\in I$, with source $C$ and target $B$. There is $R\in I$ and an $R$-algebra map $u_R:C_R\to B_R$ whose extension to $L$ is $u_L$.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras (2), the affine-algebra form of Limits Tag 01ZM (2). Directed-union verification written here.

proof.text: The map $u_R$ already respects multiplication. Let $\Delta_B:B\to B\otimes_FB$ and $\Delta_C:C\to C\otimes_FC$ be the maps corresponding to the group multiplications. Base change gives maps $\Delta_{B,R}$ and $\Delta_{C,R}$; the canonical identification $B_R\otimes_RB_R=(B\otimes_FB)\otimes_FR$ sends $(b\otimes r)\otimes(b'\otimes s)$ to $(b\otimes b')\otimes rs$, with inverse $(b\otimes b')\otimes r\mapsto(b\otimes r)\otimes(b'\otimes1)$. For every $c\in C_R$, the difference between $\Delta_{B,R}(u_R(c))$ and $(u_R\otimes_Ru_R)(\Delta_{C,R}(c))$ becomes zero over $L$, since $j'$ is a group homomorphism. For any $F$-vector space $V$, choosing an $F$-basis identifies $V\otimes_FR\to V\otimes_FL$ with a direct sum of the injective map $R\hookrightarrow L$, hence it is injective. Apply this with $V=B\otimes_FB$ to show that the difference is zero already over $R$. This proves the multiplication equation for $\operatorname{Spec}u_R$. The base-changed group laws satisfy their identities because each identity over $F$ remains an identity after applying the functor of base change. No test on geometric points is used.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; Tag 01JX, base change. Agent-written tensor calculation and basis argument.

proof.text: Choose finitely many algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ over $F$. Surjectivity of $u_L$ gives $z_i\in C\otimes_FL$ with $u_L(z_i)=b_i\otimes1$. Express each $z_i$ as a finite sum $\sum_a c_{ia}\otimes\ell_{ia}$ and enlarge $R$ by the finitely many coefficients $\ell_{ia}$. The $z_i$ then lie in $C_R$, and the same equations hold in $B_R$: their differences vanish in $B\otimes_FL$, while $B_R\to B\otimes_FL$ is injective by the basis argument of step 4 with $V=B$. Thus every generator $b_i\otimes1$ is in the image of $u_R$, as are all scalars of $R$; therefore $u_R$ is surjective. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}u_R:G_R\to H_R$ is a closed immersion. The multiplication equation of step 4 remains true after this enlargement by functoriality. This finite choice also works for $n=0$, when the scalars alone generate $B_R$.

source.place: Finite-generator proof of the surjectivity-spreading argument underlying Limits Tag 01ZP, lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation; affine criterion Morphisms Tag 01QO.

proof.text: The ring $R$ is nontrivial since it is a subring of the field $L$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-maximal-ideal] choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset R$. It gives a closed point $x$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$: its closure consists of primes containing $\mathfrak m$, hence only $\mathfrak m$. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is of finite type over $F$, and $F$ is algebraically closed, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] identifies the structural map $F\to\kappa(x)$ with an isomorphism. Composing $R\to\kappa(x)$ with its inverse gives an $F$-algebra map $a:R\to F$. Base change $\operatorname{Spec}u_R$ along $\operatorname{Spec}a$. It is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. For $A=B,C$, the isomorphism $(A\otimes_FR)\otimes_{R,a}F\simeq A$ sends $(v\otimes r)\otimes t$ to $v\,a(r)t$, with inverse $v\mapsto(v\otimes1)\otimes1$. These maps commute with the multiplications since they are the base-change identifications. The multiplication equation of step 4 therefore specializes to a group homomorphism $j:G\to H$. This is the required embedding; no claim identifies its $L$-extension with the originally supplied $j'$.
